Extremely tasteful buffet
Oct 2025 • Family
Extremely tasteful buffet with many things to choose from. Seafood, sushi, vietnamese food, beef, salads, desserts. Something for everybody for sure. Everything was high quality and tasty. Even wines (two or three to choose from, but they were ok).

Wanted the payment in cash, which was a bit odd for a Finn since we havent used cash in many, many years.

Service was careless and dismissive from start to finish. Hospitality seems like an afterthought here.
Jun 2025 • Couples
Our dinner at Poseidon Da Nang was, without exaggeration, one of the most uncomfortable and frustrating dining experiences I have had in recent memory. What made it so disappointing was not the food itself, but the consistently careless and at times condescending behavior of the staff. From the moment we arrived, it was clear that hospitality was not a priority at this location.

We had made a reservation for 7:30 PM and arrived on time. After confirming our details with the front desk, a staff member in a white shirt showed us to our table and told us we could begin helping ourselves to the buffet. Within just a few minutes, as we returned to the table with our first plate, we found another staff member in a red shirt leading a large family to that same table. When we explained that we had already been seated there, he simply told us we had not. He made no effort to confirm the situation and offered no courtesy or explanation, leaving us standing there confused. We eventually had to wave down the original staff member, who then moved us to another table. While he later apologized on the other staff’s behalf, it came too late. The entire interaction had already made us feel as though we were the problem, when we had done nothing wrong.

Service did not improve from there. No one came by to check on us or offer water or basic assistance. We had to flag someone down just to ask for two bottles of water, crab gloves, and one pressed pineapple juice with no sugar. The staff member in red responded with a blank stare, clearly unsure of what we were asking. Only one bottle of water was brought to the table. It was again the staff member in white who had to step in and confirm the order for us.

When the juice was delivered, I tasted it and felt it was sweet, so I asked whether it truly had no sugar. The white-shirted staff assured me it did not. Ten minutes later, another juice appeared without explanation. We told the staff we had already received one, and they quietly took it away. Shortly after, the same red-shirted staff member returned and told us the first juice did in fact contain sugar, and the second was the correct one. Despite the confusion and the error being entirely on their side, both drinks appeared on our bill. When we pointed this out, rather than correcting the charge, they asked if we had consumed both — completely missing the point.

Throughout the meal, the same red-shirted staff member repeatedly looked over at our table, laughing and talking with colleagues while glancing in our direction. It created an atmosphere that felt less like a dining experience and more like we were being watched or talked about. No one came by to clear our plates or check on us. Then, toward the end of the meal, the same staff member approached us and asked whether we knew how much it cost to dine there. This was after another staff member had already explained the pricing in detail at the beginning. The question was unnecessary and condescending, and it left a lasting impression that we were being judged.

To his credit, the white-shirted staff member did attempt to make up for the behavior of the others. He was polite, attentive, and seemed to genuinely want to help. Unfortunately, his efforts could not undo the damage caused by the rest of the team. What we experienced was not simply bad service. It was a consistent pattern of unprofessionalism, poor communication, and an absence of the most basic level of respect for guests.

I have dined at the Poseidon location in Ho Chi Minh City with my family and was treated with courtesy and care. The Da Nang location was a stark contrast. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone, and I sincerely hope management reconsiders how this branch is being run. If what we experienced is considered acceptable, then Poseidon Da Nang has fundamentally lost sight of what hospitality means.
